title: private-deploy networking incident breadcrumbs
content:
Context:
- Customer private deployment (VPC-peered with our control plane) started failing to download models and call upstream hosted services intermittently.
- Symptoms: model fetch (s3-compatible) 502/504s from runtime, occasional TLS handshake failures when connecting to control plane, intermittent DNS resolution failures for internal control-plane hostname (controlplane.internal.redwood).
- Affected: 3 nodes in customer-prod cluster (k8s), all in same AZ.
- Incident started ~2026-02-23 22:10 UTC.

Repro / first triage steps taken (raw commands & outputs):
1) Check pod logs (runtime pod):
  kubectl -n redwood get pods -o wide | grep runtime
  kubectl -n redwood logs runtime-0 --since=1h > ~/tmp/runtime-logs.txt
  # observed repeated: "error fetching model: lease timeout, upstream read aborted" and TLS handshake error: "tls: handshake failure"

2) DNS checks from node and pod:
  # from node (host):
  dig +short controlplane.internal.redwood @10.0.0.2
  # -> sometimes returns IP (10.100.5.12), sometimes empty. TTL low (~5s).

  # from pod:
  kubectl exec -n redwood -it runtime-0 -- nslookup controlplane.internal.redwood || true
  Server: 10.96.0.10
  Address: 10.96.0.10#53

  Name: controlplane.internal.redwood
  Address: 10.100.5.12
  # then immediately: 
  ;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached

3) TCP connectivity to control plane IP (when DNS resolved):
  kubectl exec -n redwood runtime-0 -- bash -c "curl -v https://10.100.5.12:443/healthz --resolve controlplane.internal.redwood:443:10.100.5.12" 2>&1 | sed -n '1,120p'
  * Rebuilt URL to: https://10.100.5.12/healthz
  * TLS 1.3 handshake error: error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number
  # hypothesis: client using TLS1.3, server expects different cipher / SNI mismatch?

4) VPC peering / routing checks (AWS):
  # checked route tables for customer VPC and control plane VPC; peering exists (pcx-0a1b2c3d)
  aws ec2 describe-vpc-peering-connections --filters Name=status-code,Values=active --query 'VpcPeeringConnections[?VpcPeeringConnectionId==`pcx-0a1b2c3d`].{AccepterVpc:AccepterVpcInfo.VpcId,RequesterVpc:RequesterVpcInfo.VpcId}'
  # routes: route table rtb-0807 has route to 10.100.0.0/16 via pcx-0a1b2c3d
  # BUT note: customer had a more specific route for 10.100.5.0/24 pointing to a TGW attachment -> possible overlapping route precedence

5) Packet captures (tcpdump) on node ENI and inside pod (via hostNetwork debug pod):
  # on host ENI (eth0): sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 host 10.100.5.12 and port 443 -w /tmp/tcpdump-host.pcap
  # inside pod (sidecar debug): tcpdump -n -i any host 10.100.5.12 and port 443 -w /tmp/tcpdump-pod.pcap
  # Observed: SYN from pod reaches 10.100.5.12, SYN-ACK returned, but some SYN-ACKs not observed on host ENI (possible asymmetric routing).

6) Traceroute from node to controlPlane IP:
  sudo traceroute -n 10.100.5.12
  1  10.0.1.1  0.6 ms
  2  10.2.0.1  1.0 ms
  3  10.100.5.12  2.2 ms
  # traceroute looks direct via peering, but intermittent packet loss seen.

7) Verify security groups / NACLs:
  # security groups on control plane ENIs allow customer CIDR 10.0.0.0/16: ingress TCP 443 ALLOW. Egress rules wide open.
  # NACLs for subnet are default / allow.

8) Check CoreDNS metrics & logs (k8s cluster):
  kubectl -n kube-system logs -l k8s-app=kube-dns --since=2h
  # CoreDNS shows repeated timeouts forwarding queries to 10.0.0.2 (customer DNS forwarder). Heapster reports increased latency.

9) Egress/NAT check (customer nodes in private subnet use NAT gateway for internet):
  # curl to s3-compatible upstream sometimes times out; checking NAT gw CloudWatch shows intermittent high latency and occasional status check failures in same time window.

10) TLS certs & SNI check:
  openssl s_client -connect 10.100.5.12:443 -servername controlplane.internal.redwood -tls1_2 -msg
  # handshake succeeds with TLS1.2 and cert CN=controlplane.internal.redwood, SAN includes internal name.
  openssl s_client -connect 10.100.5.12:443 -servername controlplane.internal.redwood -tls1_3
  # handshake fails with "wrong version number" on some attempts.
  # server appears to support TLS1.2 & some TLS1.3, but intermittently failing during TLS1.3 negotiation. Could be middlebox (ALB with TLS offload) or MTU/fragmentation issue.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Asymmetric routing due to overlapping route tables (TGW vs VPC peering). SYN reaches server but return path uses TGW -> dropped or goes to different routing plane, causing intermittent connection failures and inconsistent DNS responses.
2) Customer DNS forwarder (10.0.0.2) is overloaded or intermittently dropping UDP queries -> CoreDNS falls back and shows timeouts. Low TTL on the internal hosted zone exacerbates flapping.
3) TLS handshake failures caused by middlebox (L7 load balancer / ALB) misconfiguration or a TLS offload device; could be negotiating TLS1.3 and falling back inconsistently.
4) NAT gateway intermittent issues causing egress failures to model repo (s3) and other external services.
5) Security group rules or NACLs misapplied for a subset of AZs (less likely, checks look clean).

Next actions / playbook items (what to try & who to involve):
- Networking: Confirm route priority and overlapping routes. Ask infra-customer to dump route tables for VPC, TGW attachments, and peering routes for affected subnets (assigned to Samir). (ticket NET-7213)
- Control plane owners: check ALB / NLB config and TLS policy; enable debug logging on ALB (Maya). Verify listeners support TLS1.3 properly or force TLS1.2 for a test window.
- Customer: ask them to run tcpdump on their side of peering for time window to confirm return path. (Leah to coordinate)
- Increase CoreDNS forwarder capacity / switch pod to use stub domain pointing directly to control plane IPs temporarily to reduce UDP forwarder dependence.
- Short-term mitigation: add route-based fallback to route controlplane.internal.redwood to a different control-plane replica in another AZ/region (if available) and pin runtime to TLS1.2 for model fetches.
- Add long-packet-reassembly / increase MTU checks: try lowering pod MTU to 1300 on a test node to see if TLS1.3 fragmentation issue disappears.

Notes / miscellaneous observations:
- Observed TTL on DNS records low (~5s): likely TTL configured to force fast failover, but causes flapping when forwarders are intermittent.
- Customer reported a recent config change to TGW route propagation on 2026-02-22 04:30 UTC - timeline aligns with incident.
- Past incidents: see NET-5091 (2016-11) - similar pattern, resolved by removing more specific overlapping route.

Commands to run next (copy-paste):
# Route dump (customer-side):
aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-0abcde12345 --query 'RouteTables[*].{id:RouteTableId,routes:Routes}' > ~/tmp/customer-route-tables.json

# tcpdump on customer ENI (ask customer):
sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 host 10.100.5.12 and port 443 -w /tmp/peer-side.pcap

# force runtime to use TLS1.2 for model fetch (test):
# set env var in runtime deployment: RUNTIME_TLS_MIN=TLS1.2 then rollout restart deployment/runtime
kubectl -n redwood set env deployment/runtime RUNTIME_TLS_MIN=TLS1_2 && kubectl -n redwood rollout restart deployment/runtime

# temporarily point CoreDNS stub to control plane IPs (test):
# edit Corefile to add:
# controlplane.internal.redwood:53 {
#     forward . 10.100.5.12 10.100.5.13
# }

Timeline notes (short):
- 2026-02-22 04:30 UTC: Customer applied TGW route propagation change (suspected)
- 2026-02-23 22:10 UTC: First customer alert - intermittent model fetch failures
- 2026-02-24 02:00 UTC: Eng began triage; initial DNS flapping observed
- 2026-02-25 08:00 UTC: Found overlapping route pointing to TGW for specific /24 (suspicious)
- 2026-02-25 -> today: ongoing, mitigation in progress (forcing TLS1.2 for a test, requesting route table change)

Immediate asks:
- Samir: get route table and TGW attachment dump from customer + confirm whether they rolled back the 02/22 change.
- Maya: check control plane ALB TLS policy + server logs for handshake errors (timestamps above).
- Leah: coordinate customer tcpdump and confirm VPC side ENI logs.

Open questions / things to verify later:
- Is there an inline firewall / third-party appliance inserted via TGW attachments that rewrites packets or does TLS offload?
- Are there any cross-account routing policies that could cause return traffic to egress through a different path?
- If TLS1.3 fragmentation is the issue, why does TLS1.2 succeed consistently? Need to compare packet sizes and MSS.

References / related tickets:
- NET-7213 (current)
- NET-5091 (historic similar)
- Confluence runbook (linked above)

Notes-to-self: keep raw captures archived under /shared/incident-captures/NET-7213 and timestamp filename pattern. When we have pcap from both sides, run tcptrace/wireshark and compare sequence numbers to confirm asymmetric routing.

-- Oliver
